findings.claim: _resolve_until builds the deadline with naive local-time arithmetic (now.replace(hour=..., minute=...)), which doesn't account for DST transitions. On a fall-back night, a --until time inside the repeated hour (e.g. 01:30 when clocks fall back at 02:00) is reached the first time wall-clock hits it, so run_batch's clock() >= until check (also naive datetime.now()) stops the batch roughly an hour earlier than the operator intended; on a spring-forward night a --until time inside the skipped hour is never observed exactly and is only caught once the clock reaches the post-jump time. This is real but affects at most two nights a year and only when --until falls in the transition hour, so it's not worth blocking on.

The docstring at cli.py:532-536 justifies `outcome.state = result.state` by claiming it changes what `run_batch`'s breaker sees ('rather than the pre-packaging READY_FOR_REVIEW every packaged task would otherwise report to the breaker'). But `saffron/batch.py`'s `ABORT_STATES` is `{GATE_ERROR, PREFLIGHT_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED}`, and `package_phase.package` only ever returns `state` of `READY_FOR_REVIEW` or `MERGE_FAILED` — neither of which is ever in `ABORT_STATES`. So the overwrite has no effect on `consecutive_aborts` either way; the stated rationale for the line is false, even though the line itself is harmless (it only affects an object no other code reads after this call returns).

No test drives `saffron batch` with a real `--until` value through `main()` and checks what reaches `run_batch`; `test_a_deadline_earlier_than_now_resolves_to_tomorrow` only calls the pure `_resolve_until` helper directly, and `test_saffron_batch_runs_a_night_with_the_defaults_4_2_1_fixes` only exercises the `--until`-omitted (`None`) branch. Replacing this line with `until = None` (silently ignoring the flag) — or swapping the two arguments passed to `_resolve_until`, which would raise on the very first real `--until` invocation — leaves every test in the diff green, because nothing in the suite ever supplies `--until` to the `batch` subcommand and inspects the resulting deadline. The one call site that turns the CLI's `--until` string into the datetime `run_batch` actually compares against is untested, even though it is the exact usage shown in §4.2.1's own example invocation.

probe.find: until = _resolve_until(args.until, datetime.now()) if args.until else None
